title: Adaptive micro-batch shaping with sequence-aware truncation and prefix coalescing
creator: Maya Chen
description: Reduce wasted padding and improve end-to-end token cost by dynamically re-shaping micro-batches at the prefill->decode boundary. This ticket implements a sequence-aware bucketizer that considers runtime kernel characteristics (kernel warmup cost, quantized kernel throughput at different seqlens), merges short-prefix requests into coalesced prefill groups when safe, and applies conservative truncation/soft-trimming heuristics to limit extreme pad inflation. Goal: reduce average padded tokens per request by >=20% on conversational workloads while keeping p99 latency regression <= 5ms and preserving model output quality.
acceptance_criteria: Integration with serving runtime to produce per-request bucket assignments and a re-bucketing pass at the prefill->decode transition
Observed >=20% reduction in padded tokens per request on ’chat-heavy’ test corpus (internal dataset) under default routing policies
p99 latency change <= +5ms and mean latency neutral or improved in canary traffic (10% traffic) for common instance types
No measurable degradation in top-level quality checks (ROUGE / semantic similarity on eval prompts) beyond noise; regression alerting wired to console
Config flags exposed: enable/disable prefix-coalesce, conservative_truncation_ratio, kernel_hint_tuning (defaults safe for Hosted tier)
implementation_plan: Design bucketizer: histogram of sequence lengths + kernel-performance model -> cost-per-token estimate per kernel variant
Add prefill->decode re-bucketing hook in request path: compute candidate micro-batches and apply prefix-coalescing rules

Prefix coalescing strategy: only merge requests that share the same model/version, identical special-token handling, and compatible top-k/frequency sampling settings; limit merged group max combined prompt tokens
Introduce soft-truncation: probabilistic trimming of trailing whitespace/low-importance tokens guided by a cheap heuristic scorer to avoid output regressions
Expose tuning knobs in Console and add canary rollout mode with traffic shaping and automatic fallback to original bucketing on SLA breaches
Add kernel-hint metadata emitted with each micro-batch for kernel selector to prefer warm/quantized kernels when beneficial
End-to-end CI perf test and new Grafana dashboard panels for padded-tokens, per-seqlen kernel selection, and canary SLOs
experiments_and_results: Synthetic chat corpus (20k requests): baseline average padded tokens = 142; after shaping = 108 (-23.9%)
Throughput on g5.12xlarge (mixed-precision kernels): tokens/sec +12% for steady-state workload when groups are coherent
p99 latency measured in preliminary canary (5% traffic): baseline 62ms -> 64.7ms (+2.7ms), within target
Worst-case sample: a pathological multi-prefix burst increased scheduling jitter — added safety cap on merged group size to avoid this
Mini A/B quality sweep (500 prompts): semantic similarity delta = -0.004 (within noise); one prompt showed truncation edge-case fixed by relaxing truncation threshold
tradeoffs: Merging prefixes improves kernel utilization but adds risk of cross-request interference (memory pressure on KV cache) — mitigated by strict compatibility checks
Soft-truncation reduces padded compute but can change model output; we bias toward conservative defaults and route sensitive customers to opt-out
Kernel-hinting complexity: adds metadata and scheduling coupling between runtime and kernel selector; however it enables better throughput/latency choices for quantized kernels
Increased scheduler CPU work per request for re-bucketing; measured overhead ~0.6ms/request — acceptable given token-cost savings for common workloads
rollout_plan: Local unit + integration tests -> runtime branch with feature flag (microbatch_shaping_v2)
Benchmark cluster run (perf infra) comparing baseline vs shaping across 3 instance types (g5, a100, t4)
Canary rollout: 1% traffic -> monitor padded_tokens, per-route p99 latency, error rates for 48h
Expand to 10% if SLOs stable, run 7-day canary, then 50%/100% with automatic fallback if SLOs triggered
Post-rollout: collect cost delta, update Optimize recommendations to suggest shaping for eligible workloads
dependencies: PM-442 (Console flag UX for advanced runtime knobs)
